title: Common prohibited uses across three providers

opening.headline: When there is confusion about whether AI can be used in work, the boundary is judged based on the categories commonly prohibited by the three companies' usage policies.
body: Drafting customer response text using AI seems like a good idea. It is somewhat uneasy to have AI filter out applicant documents, and it is even more unsettling to have AI determine the results of personnel evaluations. If you replace this vague feeling with the standards stated in the policy document, judgment becomes much easier.

In this class, we will first look at how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic's usage policies are structured. We then look for prohibited categories that appear in common across the three documents, identifying high-risk areas and implications for user responsibility. Lastly, by solving customer service and personnel evaluation cases, you will learn how to classify in-house uses into permitted, cautioned, and prohibited.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: The common prohibited categories of the three companies' usage policies can be explained.
In-house use can be categorized as permitted, cautioned, or prohibited.

screens.title: Can I use this for work?
screens.lead: Read the three work scenes and intuitively decide whether each can be left to AI.

visual.alt: An illustration of three situation cards laid out horizontally: customer service, applicant document filing, and personnel evaluation comment.

paragraphs: Creating a draft of customer service text using AI doesn't seem to be a problem. This is because people read it, refine it, and then send it. On the other hand, having AI filter out applicant documents is somewhat uneasy. Because one person’s chance is at stake.

Having AI determine personnel evaluation comments is even more unsettling. This is because it directly affects how people are treated. You need to be able to explain where this feeling comes from so you can judge it on the same basis as your teammates.
Getting a feel for where the boundaries are before reading each company's policy line by line will make it clear what to look for when reading the policy document.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Why does anxiety increase in these three scenes? Is it because the results are different or because the people affected are different?

screens.outro: In order to turn vague anxiety into a policy standard, let me first recall my own experience.

screens.title: This is a task that I felt I should not be asked to do.
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Are there any tasks that you felt should not be given to AI?
items.answer: Such intuitions are usually well founded. A policy is a document that organizes these intuitions into sentences. No matter what task comes to mind, if you think about why you felt that way, you can find out which category of policy it connects to.

items.prompt: Was it more of a legal issue that made you feel that way?
items.answer: Uses that violate the law are commonly prohibited under the policies of all three companies. This includes uses that assist in illegal activities or infringe upon the intellectual property rights of others.

items.prompt: Was it because of privacy or impact on people?
items.answer: Using personal data without consent leads to the category of rights violations, and AI determining the treatment of people leads to the problem of automated decisions in high-risk areas. In both cases, this is the topic that the policy directly addresses.

screens.outro: Now that we're ready to connect our intuition and policy categories, let's start with what a policy is: a document.

screens.title: What is the Usage Policy: Structure of the Three Companies
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare the structure of the three companies' usage policies.

visual.alt: An illustration showing three columns of OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic side by side, each column showing the document name and organization.
labels: Protecting people, respecting privacy, protecting minors, empowering people
Google Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy
Common Sense: Illegality, Infringement, Security Violation, Harm, Deception

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body: OpenAI's Usage policies begin with the stance of ensuring that products are used safely and responsibly while ensuring maximum user control. The rules are divided into large bundles: protecting people, respecting privacy, protecting minors, and empowering people. Please note that if you violate or circumvent our policies, you may lose access or face other penalties. We also clarify that these rules do not replace legal requirements, professional duties, or ethical responsibilities.

tabs.label: Google
tabs.body: Google lists its prohibited practices in a numbered list under the name Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy. The first is dangerous or illegal activities, the second is security violations of other services, the third is sexual, violent and hateful activities, and the fourth is false information and deception. At the end, it is written that exceptions may be made for educational, documentary, scientific or artistic considerations or when there is greater public interest.

tabs.label: Anthropic
tabs.body: Anthropic's Usage Policy is divided into three parts. There are universal standards that apply to all users and uses, high-risk use requirements that apply to specific uses that pose a high risk of harm to individuals, and additional case guidance that applies to some uses, such as consumer chatbots and agents. This policy does not ban any industry entirely, but rather focuses on how products are used.

screens.outro: Now that we have the structure in place, let's put the items from the three documents side by side and look for common prohibited categories.

screens.title: Common prohibition categories for the three policies
screens.lead: The table below shows items from the three documents side by side, grouped into five common categories. Read horizontally and make sure that although the wording is different, it covers the same topic.

data.notes: Although the three documents have different numbers of sentences and items, the above five stems appear in common. The detailed scope and exceptions vary from company to company, so if you are caught off guard in actual work, check the original policy of the service you are using.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the common categories, let's look at the high-risk uses and user responsibilities that are especially important to your business.

screens.title: High Risk Use and User Responsibility
screens.lead: Select and expand each item to see how each company addresses high-risk usage.

items.title: Google: Automated determination of high-risk areas
items.body: Google prohibits automated decisions that significantly disadvantage individuals' rights without human oversight in high-risk areas such as employment, healthcare, finance, legal, housing, insurance, and social services. The key conditions are lack of human supervision and significant disadvantages to individuals.

items.title: OpenAI: High-stakes decisions without human review
items.body: OpenAI places a ban on automating high-risk decisions without human review in sensitive areas. Those areas include employment, finance and credit, insurance, law, health care, housing, and education. We also do not permit the provision of licensed legal or medical advice without the involvement of a professional.

items.title: Anthropic: High-Risk Use Requirements
items.body: Anthropic imposes a high-risk use requirement that sets aside certain uses that are likely to cause harm to individuals. A structural feature is that more specific requirements are imposed rather than universal standards that are commonly applied to all users.

items.title: User Responsibilities
items.body: OpenAI states that its rules do not replace legal requirements, professional obligations, or ethical responsibilities. Compliance with the policy does not eliminate responsibility. What the tool allows is separate from what our organization is responsible for, and that is your responsibility.

screens.outro: Now that we've organized the categories and responsibilities, let's apply them to an example.

screens.title: Commentary: Why are customer service and personnel evaluations handled differently?
screens.lead: The instructor compares and answers the two cases using the same questions. Select the right arrow to see the steps one by one.

steps.title: Stage 1 Affected Persons
steps.body: Drafts of customer service text are read, polished and sent by humans. Even if the draft is wrong, it can be corrected before sending, and the decision does not disadvantage any specific individual. Personnel evaluations directly affect the treatment of the employees being evaluated.

steps.title: Level 2 area
steps.body: Personnel evaluation is an employment area. This is an area that both Google and OpenAI's policies consider as high-risk areas. Even for the same AI tool, the level of attention required by policy varies depending on the area in which it is used.

steps.title: 3rd level decision
steps.body: When AI sets evaluation grades or makes decisions that disadvantage individuals, it becomes closer to making automatic decisions without human supervision. This is where the policy becomes problematic. The issue is who makes the decisions.

steps.title: Step 4: Human Role
steps.body: Even in the same personnel task, refining the sentences of comments written by an evaluator and AI determining the evaluation results are different. In the previous case, humans make the judgment and AI helps with expression. In the latter case, the judgment itself is handed over to AI.

steps.title: Level 5 judgment
steps.body: The customer response draft is close to acceptable. Care must be taken when organizing sentences in evaluation comments. Having AI determine the evaluation results goes against the purpose of the policy. Even if a person only formally approves at the end, if the actual judgment is made by AI, it is difficult to consider it as human supervision.

screens.outro: Now that you understand the difference between the two cases, let's organize them into a table that distinguishes their in-house use.

screens.title: Explanation: Divide in-house uses into permitted, cautionary, and prohibited
screens.lead: The instructor explains the process of dividing company usage into three categories. Select the right arrow to check each space one by one.

steps.title: allow
steps.body: It is used for purposes such as summarizing meeting minutes, refining sentences, and organizing ideas, where a person can check the results and there is no disadvantage to the individual. Because it is structured so that people read and take responsibility for the results, it is far from an area that policy issues.

steps.title: caution
steps.body: Contains personal information or is intended to provide legal, medical, or financial advice. In this case, an expert review is required and the data you enter must be checked in advance. The policy specifically cautions against providing licensed advice without professional involvement.

steps.title: prohibited
steps.body: Illegal activities, security breaches, use to deceive people, and automated decisions that disadvantage individuals without human supervision are on the prohibited side. Since the three companies' policies cover common categories, you will get answers in the same direction no matter which tool you use.

steps.title: When the boundaries are ambiguous
steps.body: I ask three questions: Who is affected? Can the results be reversed? Do people make the final decision? Even though the policy is expressed differently from company to company, the answer to this question is the same. If the answer is unclear, do not leave it as Allow, but place it in the Caution box and consult with an expert or the department in charge.

screens.outro: Now that we've completed the division table, let's summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaway: Although the expressions are different, the category of prohibition is common.
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class. See how the vague anxiety you felt at first has changed.

paragraphs: Although OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic's usage policies are structured and worded differently, they have common categories of prohibition: unlawful conduct, infringement of rights, security breach, harm, and deception. So, no matter which company's tool you use, you can check its purpose based on these five stems.

Automated decisions without human oversight are particularly problematic in high-risk areas such as employment, healthcare, finance, and law. Compliance with the policy does not eliminate legal and professional responsibility. Therefore, business uses are divided into allowable, cautionary, and prohibited, and boundaries ask who is affected, the possibility of reversal, and the person's final judgment.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: What a tool allows and what responsibilities our organization takes on are two different things.

checks.intro: Try to summarize what you just learned by pairing examples with common categories. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: Match the following examples of prohibited behavior with the appropriate common category.
left: Use of personal data without consent
Malicious code creation and unauthorized access
right: Infringement of the rights of others
checks.explain: Although the three policies are expressed differently, they have a common thread of violation of law, violation of rights, violation of security, harm, and deception.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: What is the core reason why letting AI determine employee evaluation grades goes against the purpose of the policy?
options: This is because the evaluation document is long and difficult for AI to process.
This is because AI cannot be used in any form for human resources work.
This is because the quality of sentences is lower than that of customer service.
This is because employment is a high-risk area and decisions are made automatically without human supervision.
checks.explain: Employment is a high-risk area, and when AI makes decisions that disadvantage individuals without human supervision, it is close to being automated. The task of refining the sentences written by the evaluator is viewed differently.

wrong.0: The issue is not processing power, but the impact on individuals and whether or not there is human supervision.
wrong.1: Even in the same personnel work, it can be used with caution for purposes that require human judgment, such as refining comments and sentences.
wrong.2: The issue is not the quality of the sentence, but who has the power to make the decision.

glossary.def: This is a rule document set by the provider on how to use the product and what not to do.

Even though the wording varies from company to company, these are prohibited areas that are common to all three policies: illegality, infringement of rights, security infringement, harm, and deception.
It is used in areas where going wrong can have a significant impact on individuals, such as employment, healthcare, finance, and law.
The principle is that even if the policy is followed, legal obligations and professional responsibility remain with the user.

misconceptions.myth: If it is not written in the policy, you can do it.
misconceptions.fact: Policies are only minimum standards. Legal requirements, professional duties and ethical responsibilities remain separate from policy.

misconceptions.myth: Since it is a result created by AI, if a problem arises, the AI company is responsible.
misconceptions.fact: The policy assumes that users use responsibly, and states that inappropriate use may result in liability, such as access restrictions. The people and organizations that use it are responsible.

misconceptions.myth: It is not an automatic decision when a person just presses the approve button at the end.
misconceptions.fact: If the actual judgment is made by AI and the person only gives formal approval, it is difficult to consider it as human supervision. People must be able to understand and judge the content.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Policies have common prohibition categories, even if wording varies from company to company.
Human supervision is key in high-risk areas.
Complying with the policy and user responsibilities are separate.
Boundaries ask who will be affected, the likelihood of reversal, and the person's final judgment.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What uses of our work require attention, and where should people make their decisions?
